sources.title: Enforcement programme: Industry's failure to implement One Touch Switch by deadline of 3 April 2023
sources.evidence_location: official HTML case status and closing text
sources.geography: United Kingdom fixed broadband and landline providers
facts: The case opened on 3 April 2023
The case closed on 11 June 2026
Providers were required to implement One Touch Switch by 3 April 2023
The page cites General Conditions C7.18 to C7.27
limitations: A closed enforcement programme does not prove every switch is problem-free
Regulatory compliance evidence is not network coverage

sources.title: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business
sources.evidence_location: official HTML takeover and no-takeover sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom broadband and landline customers
facts: A takeover should usually allow existing service to continue
Existing contracts should usually transfer to the new provider
Material contract changes can permit exit without an early termination charge
If there is no takeover the service will stop on a notified date
limitations: Provider failure status does not identify alternative service availability

sources.title: Ofcom fines Virgin Media £28m for repeatedly preventing customers from cancelling contracts
facts: Ofcom imposed a £28 million fine
The decision was published on 8 July 2026
Ofcom found unreasonable effort and difficulty in cancellation calls
The findings included call dropping, transfers and unnecessary holds
limitations: The enforcement outcome does not prove local broadband quality
Provider conduct evidence is not parcel coverage

sources.title: Changing provider
sources.evidence_location: official HTML slamming and attempted-slamming sections
facts: The page explains slamming and attempted slamming
A customer should contact the former provider after an unauthorised switch
The customer should also contact the acquiring provider
An attempted unauthorised switch can be cancelled through the current provider
limitations: Complaint guidance does not establish the facts of an individual case
Switching disputes are not service-availability evidence

sources.title: About us - Building Digital UK
sources.evidence_location: Project Gigabit and Shared Rural Network sections
facts: BDUK is responsible for gigabit-capable broadband rollout and 4G expansion in hard-to-reach areas
Project Gigabit targets premises outside supplier commercial plans
The government expects 99% gigabit-capable coverage by 2032
The Shared Rural Network is described as benefiting an extra 280,000 premises and 16,000 kilometres of roads
limitations: National programme targets are not current parcel coverage
Expected future coverage and programme benefit remain aggregate
